item.title: Study finds satellite radar warming could cut high-risk bridge counts by a third
item.description: A global study of 744 long-span bridges has found that structures in North America face the highest risk of geo-hazard-related damage anywhere on Earth, with many built during a 1960s construction boom now nearing or surpassing their intended lifespans. The research, published this week in Nature Communications, proposes satellite radar imaging as a tool to monitor aging infrastructure and reduce the number of bridges classified as high risk.

item.title: NATO intercepts second Iranian missile in Turkish airspace
item.description:
NATO air defense systems shot down a second Iranian ballistic missile in Turkish airspace on Monday, the Turkish Ministry of National Defense confirmed, as debris rained down on uninhabited fields in the southeastern province of Gaziantep. The interception, which occurred at approximately 3:00 p.m. local time, marks the second such incident in five days and deepens a crisis that has drawn the Western alliance closer to direct involvement in the widening U.S.-Iran conflict.

Hours later, the U.S. State Department ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave the American consulate in Adana, near the strategic Incirlik Air Base, citing safety risks. Americans in southeastern Turkey were "strongly encouraged to depart now," the department said in an updated travel advisory.

item.title: UN chief to argue Iran war bolsters case for renewables
item.description:
As the U.S.-Israeli air campaign against Iran enters its second week, the conflict's disruption to global fossil fuel supplies has intensified a debate over whether the crisis could accelerate the world's transition to renewable energy. With approximately 20% of global crude oil and natural gas supply suspended and oil prices climbing to their highest levels since 2022, energy experts, world leaders, and industry groups are making the case that homegrown clean power is not just a climate imperative but a matter of national security.

U.N. Secretary-General António Guterres plans to press that argument on Monday. "The turmoil we are witnessing today in the Middle East makes it evident that we are facing a global energy system largely tied to fossil fuels — where supply is concentrated in a few regions and every conflict risks sending shock waves through the global economy," Guterres said in an email to The Associated Press. "In past oil shocks, countries had little choice but to absorb the pain. Now they have an exit ramp."

item.title: G7 fails to agree on oil reserve release as crude tops $100
item.description:
Finance ministers from the Group of Seven nations held an emergency call Monday morning to discuss the historic surge in oil prices but failed to reach consensus on a joint release of strategic petroleum reserves, with France saying the bloc is "not there yet" on organizing a global drawdown.

French Finance Minister Roland Lescure made the remarks after the virtual meeting, according to Bloomberg, which reported that the G7 is "not there yet" in terms of a coordinated release of emergency oil inventories despite the escalating crisis triggered by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

item.title: Greek tanker exits Hormuz with Saudi crude as traffic slowly resumes
item.description:
A Greek-operated oil tanker carrying a million barrels of Saudi crude has become one of the first large vessels to exit the Persian Gulf since the Strait of Hormuz was effectively shut down by Iranian attacks more than a week ago, according to Bloomberg, even as the vast majority of shipping operators remain unwilling to risk the passage.

The Shenlong, operated by Greece's Dynacom Tankers Management Ltd., switched off its transponder in the Persian Gulf on March 4 while heading toward Hormuz and began signaling again off the coast of India on Monday morning, ship-tracking data compiled by Bloomberg showed. U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright confirmed the transit in a weekend interview with Fox News, and told CNN that a broader resumption of traffic was "not too long away," adding that the worst-case timeline was "a few weeks, that's not months".

item.title: Macron announces naval mission to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron announced Monday that France and its allies are organizing a "purely defensive" naval mission to escort commercial ships through the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway that has been effectively shut since the start of the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran on February 28.

Speaking in Cyprus after meeting with Cypriot President Nik Christodides and Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis, Macron said the escort operation "must be collaboratively prepared with both European and non-European nations" and would aim to progressively reopen the strait, through which roughly 20% of global oil production normally flows.

item.title: Iran war splits BRICS as India blocks joint response
item.description:
More than a week into the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, the BRICS coalition has failed to issue a single collective statement on a conflict engulfing one of its own members — a silence that analysts say lays bare the limits of the 11-nation bloc's ambitions to reshape the global order.

The absence of a unified response stands in contrast to June 2025, when BRICS, then under Brazil's chairmanship, swiftly condemned coordinated U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran as a violation of international law. This time, under India's rotating presidency, the organization has been conspicuously quiet since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28, killing more than 1,230 people in its first six days.

item.title: Russia says it is 'not neutral' in US-Iran war
item.description: Russia's ambassador to the United Kingdom declared on March 8 that Moscow is "not neutral" in the war between the United States and Israel on one side and Iran on the other, the most explicit public acknowledgment yet of Russia's alignment in a conflict that has reshaped the geopolitics of the Middle East in barely two weeks.

item.title: Iran war produces largest oil supply disruption in history, Rapidan Energy says
item.description:
The U.S.-Israeli war on Iran, now in its tenth day, has produced the largest oil supply disruption in recorded history, sending energy prices surging and intensifying calls from analysts and policymakers to accelerate the shift toward renewable energy sources.

Roughly 20% of global crude oil and natural gas supply has been suspended since the conflict began on February 28, according to Reuters, after Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz and attacked energy infrastructure across the Persian Gulf. Crude oil prices have climbed above $100 per barrel, with consulting firm Rapidan Energy calling the disruption nearly three times greater than the 1973 Arab oil embargo.

item.title: HSBC CEO reaffirms confidence in Gulf amid Iran war
item.description:
HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery on Monday voiced the bank's continued confidence in the Gulf region's economic prospects, making him one of the first international bank leaders to publicly address the growing crisis as the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran enters its second week.

"HSBC remains steadfast in our confidence in the GCC and in the long-term strength, resilience and promise of the region," Elhedery said in a statement, according to Reuters. "We continue to believe that the years ahead will bring renewed stability, growth, and prosperity."

item.title: US intercepts Iran signal that may activate sleeper cells abroad
item.description: Nearly two weeks into Operation Epic Fury, the joint US-Israeli air campaign that began on February 28, Iran's decentralized military doctrine is being put to its most severe test — and by several accounts, it is holding. Despite the killing of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and senior military commanders, Iran has continued launching waves of ballistic missiles and drones at targets across the Middle East, raising questions about whether airpower alone can neutralize the Islamic Republic's war-fighting capacity.

item.title: UAE calls for de-escalation after 1,400 Iranian attacks
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates on Monday called for an immediate de-escalation of the US-Israeli war with Iran and a return to negotiations, as the Gulf state disclosed it had been subjected to more than 1,400 Iranian drone and missile attacks since the conflict erupted on February 28.

"De-escalation, de-escalation, de-escalation. This is our position and we will continue to offer it," UAE Ambassador Jamal Jama al Musharakh told reporters during a press briefing at the United Nations in Geneva, according to Reuters.

item.title: Iran confirms new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei wounded in war
item.description: Iranian state television confirmed on Sunday that newly appointed Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei was wounded during the ongoing conflict with the United States and Israel, referring to him as "janbaz" — a term meaning wounded by the enemy — in what Iranian media are calling the "Ramadan war." The disclosure came just hours after the Assembly of Experts officially announced his appointment on March 8, succeeding his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the initial U.S.-Israeli strikes on February 28.

item.title: Trump and Putin discuss Iran and Ukraine in phone call
item.description:
President Donald Trump called Russian President Vladimir Putin on Monday to discuss the war in Iran and ongoing efforts to settle the conflict in Ukraine, according to the Kremlin, in what appears to be the first direct conversation between the two leaders since reports emerged that Russia has been sharing targeting intelligence with Tehran against American forces.

Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Trump initiated the call "to discuss a number of critically important topics related to current developments in the international situation," with the conversation focused on the Iran conflict and trilateral negotiations on a Ukraine settlement. Ushakov described the exchange as "businesslike, frank and constructive" and said the two presidents "have not spoken by phone for a long time and agreed to communicate with each other on a regular basis".

item.title: Trump doesn't rule out seizing Iranian oil as prices spike
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday declined to rule out the possibility that the United States could seize Iranian oil as the war against Tehran enters its second week, telling NBC News that "certainly, people have talked about it" while stopping short of endorsing such a move.

"People have thought about it, but it's too soon to talk about that," Trump said, pointing to Venezuela as a precedent where the U.S. moved to secure oil access after American forces captured President Nicolás Maduro in January. Trump touted the Venezuela operation during last month's State of the Union address, saying the U.S. had already obtained more than 80 million barrels of Venezuelan oil.

item.title: Iran says it does not want to harm 'ordinary Americans'
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared on Monday that Tehran does not wish to harm ordinary American citizens, framing the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict as a war driven by Israel and its allies in Washington rather than a quarrel with the American public.

"Iran does not want to harm ordinary Americans who overwhelmingly voted to end involvement in costly foreign wars," Araghchi wrote in a post on X. "Blame for surging gas prices, costlier mortgages, and pummeled 401(k)'s lies squarely with Israel and its dupes in Washington."

item.title: Trump calls Iran's choice of Mojtaba Khamenei 'a big mistake'
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Monday sharply condemned Iran's selection of Mojtaba Khamenei as its new supreme leader, telling NBC News that the country "made a big mistake" and casting doubt on whether the appointment would endure. "I don't know if it's going to last ... I think they made a mistake," Trump said in a phone interview.

In a separate interview with the New York Post, Trump said he was "not happy" with the 56-year-old cleric replacing his father. "Not going to tell you. I'm not happy with him," Trump said from his Doral golf club near Miami when asked about his plans regarding the younger Khamenei.

item.title: RAF Typhoons down two drones over Jordan and Bahrain
item.description: British RAF Typhoon fighter jets shot down two drones overnight, one over Jordan and another heading toward Bahrain, as the United Kingdom expanded its defensive military operations across the Gulf on the tenth day of the war between Iran and a US-Israeli coalition.

item.title: UC San Diego study finds most pandemics show no lab origins
item.description: Two studies published in the past week offer fresh perspectives on viral threats — one revealing how coronaviruses rewire human cells to speed their own replication, and another providing a genomic tool to distinguish natural outbreaks from lab-linked ones, with new molecular evidence that the 1977 "Russian flu" pandemic likely originated from a failed vaccine trial.

item.title: IRGC offers Hormuz passage to nations that expel US, Israeli envoys
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Monday offered passage through the Strait of Hormuz, starting Tuesday, to any Arab or European country that expels Israeli and U.S. ambassadors from its territory, according to Shafaq News. The proposal marks a new front in Tehran's diplomatic pressure campaign as its war with the United States and Israel enters a second week.
